events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Go to Grand Haven first.** Rating: **2 of 4 (average)**. The newest Grand Haven boat report was slow, but a mixed-method line that week rated well.
- **Fish 100 to 200 ft of water, with lines around 75 to 120 ft down**, where the DNR found the few immature salmon.
- **Start with glow spoons or white paddle/flies**, and bring glow J-plugs and white flashers for a repeat of the strong mid-September boat week.
- **St. Joseph and South Haven: rate 1 (below average) to 0 (slow).** Both had slow boat reports the last time the DNR reported.
- **Muskegon: no rating.** Its newest report is from 2023-09-06, so I can't judge current boat fishing there.

## Why
- Grand Haven had the best recent boat results, so it's my first pick. The Sept 27 report called boat action slow, but also said glow spoons and white paddle/flies "worked well" (Grand Haven, 2023-09-27), and boats were excellent there on Sept 13 (Grand Haven, 2023-09-13).
- The Sept 27 Grand Haven fish were 75 to 120 ft down in 120 to 200 ft of water, so that's where I'd set lines (Grand Haven, 2023-09-27).
- I'd expect the glow-and-white combination to stay the right pick because it's the same mix that worked both at Grand Haven and at South Haven in late September (Grand Haven, 2023-09-13; South Haven, 2022-09-28).
- St. Joseph and South Haven boats were slow on Sept 27, with only a few fish at about 110 ft or past 100 ft (South Haven and St. Joseph, 2023-09-27), so I rate them lower.

## Evidence
**Recent reports (latest Sept 27, 6 days old)**
- Grand Haven boats: slow, immature salmon 75 to 120 ft down in 120 to 200 ft of water. Unspecified-method anglers rated 3 with glow spoons and white paddle/flies (Grand Haven, 2023-09-27).
- Grand Haven boats, Sept 13: excellent (4) for Chinook and coho in the channel and in front of the pierheads, using glow J-plugs and white flashers/flies (Grand Haven, 2023-09-13).
- Grand Haven boats, Sept 20: immature salmon and lake trout 65 to 110 ft down in 100 to 200 ft; big white paddles with white or green flies worked well (Grand Haven, 2023-09-20).
- South Haven boats: slow, with a few fish around 110 ft (South Haven, 2023-09-27).
- St. Joseph boats: slow, with a few fish "well past 100 feet" (St. Joseph, 2023-09-27). Sept 13 boats rated 1, with best fishing around 110 ft (St. Joseph, 2023-09-13).
- Muskegon: no salmon reports in the last three weeks; the newest is 2023-09-06.

**Past seasons (history, not current)**
- Late September, similar water: South Haven boats rated 3 on spoons in 120 ft or deeper (2022-09-28). St. Joseph boats rated 2 at 120 ft (2022-09-21) and 1 on 2022-09-28.
- Early October, similar water: South Haven boats rated 1 (2022-10-05). St. Joseph boats rated 2 for coho and Chinook on spoons, 120 ft or deeper (2022-10-05).

**Conditions now (buoy, measured weekly averages)**
- St. Joseph (buoy 45026): 64 F, flat over the week.
- South Haven (buoy 45168): 66 F, +1 F.
- Grand Haven (buoy 45029): 67 F, +2 F. Muskegon uses the same buoy, 67 F.
- The live feed was unavailable, so these are the most recent weekly summary. There's no modeled cold-layer depth or wind forecast in this data, and I didn't use the pierhead model.

**General guidance (not from reports)**
- Michigan Sea Grant says mature Chinook in early fall tend to hold in water of 55 F or less. Current buoy temperatures (64 to 67 F) are warmer than that, so fish are likely deep. This is my inference from that guidance, not a report finding.

## Caveats
- The newest reports are 6 days old (Sept 27). Fall shifts quickly, so check the next DNR bulletin before you go.
- Ratings are judgment calls from a few reports. Grand Haven's 2 combines a slow boat week with a good week that didn't specify boat versus pier.
- No current cold-layer or wind data, so I can't check whether a north or east wind has pushed cold water in.
- Muskegon has no recent boat data, so it isn't rated.
